transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! I'm Dora, your clinical conversational agent. I'm here to help with any questions you have about your cataract surgery recovery. Do you have any questions about your surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do have a few questions. When can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can start with light gardening, such as gentle weeding or watering, about 1 week after surgery. However, it's best to avoid heavy lifting, bending, or strenuous activities for a month. Also, make sure to wear protective eyewear when gardening.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you, that's helpful. I also wanted to ask, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You should have been using preservative-free eye drops four times a day to start with. If you've been using them, keep going as prescribed. If you're running out, you can ask your GP for more. If you were using eye drops before surgery, like for glaucoma or dry eyes, it's usually safe to continue using them unless you've been told otherwise.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Got it, thank you. Another thing I'm experiencing is that I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Yes, it's normal to be a bit sensitive to light as your eyes adjust to the new lenses. If it's just mild and things seem brighter than usual, wearing sunglasses when you're outside should help. But if it's severe, or you have pain and your eye is red and painful, we may need to check it further.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Okay, thank you for explaining that. Lastly, should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's common to have blurry vision in the first week after surgery, but it should improve quickly and settle down over time. If your vision is still blurry, or getting significantly worse or blurry, we may need to check it to make sure it's okay. But most people see an improvement in their vision within a few weeks after surgery.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you so much for all the information. I have no more questions at the moment.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: All your questions have been answered. I'm glad I could help. Have a good day and take care of your eyes. .
